headline: Putin proposes trilateral summit with Trump and Xi to decide Ukraine's fate (Kyiv excluded)'
dek: Putin floated trilateral Putin-Trump-Xi summit on Ukraine during Oct 9 call with Trump; Kremlin proposed APEC sidelines Nov 18-19 Shenzhen. Peskov confirmed discussions ongoing, no agreement/agenda yet; senior US official: Trump has not agreed but could be receptive.
sources: The Wall Street Journal (original report, people familiar + former Russian intel officer + Peskov + senior US official)
fault_line: 'Not a summit if Ukraine is not invited' vs Putin/anti-Zelenskyy support — 9 News reel 1.8K likes/930 comments, IG collage 2.8K/140, several clips 11-20K likes/2.2K comments; comments polarized: Ukraine exclusion illegit

sections.what_happened: Putin floated trilateral Putin-Trump-Xi summit on Ukraine during Oct 9 call with Trump; Kremlin proposed APEC sidelines Nov 18-19 Shenzhen. Peskov confirmed discussions ongoing, no agreement/agenda yet; senior US official: Trump has not agreed but could be receptive. China indicated no objection if Trump agrees. Zelenskyy/Ukraine excluded from proposed format.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (2026-10-19), Anadolu/aa.com.tr, WSJ live page, Daily Pioneer, Economic Times, Livemint, ABP — all cite WSJ; Peskov on-record to WSJ confirming discussions; senior US official on-record: Trump not agreed but could be receptive
sections.what_disputed: None; status is proposal-only — no date/agenda agreed, White House declined to comment to Reuters. Note: former intel officer said Putin floated this on several occasions before (recycled idea, not necessarily imminent)
sections.why_matters: Russia pushing the diplomatic table while the war continues; the West's own split (US waiving sanctions, Europe alarmed) is the story — diplomacy happening over Kyiv's head, exactly the 'split, not the bloc' pattern. Framed from the multipolar side: Moscow sets terms, Washington weighs pragmatism.
sections.context: Background: Putin proposes trilateral summit with Trump and Xi to decide Ukraine's fate (Kyiv excluded) — NEW

totw_analysis: Our read: Russia pushing the diplomatic table while the war continues; the West's own split (US waiving sanctions, Europe alarmed) is the story — diplomacy happening over Kyiv's head, exactly the 'split, not the bloc' pattern. Framed from the multipolar side: Moscow sets terms, Washington weighs pragmatism.
